title: Astrid and the Spire
premise: Astrid Galloway, a temple scribe bound by debt to the Thornfell monastery, has spent years copying forbidden texts and memorizing smuggler roads to pay it off. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted, Astrid's hidden magic is exposed by a raid, and they flee into the mountains with a disgraced royal cartographer named Sef, whose maps hide a secret: the king has been replaced by a crown-bound entity that feeds on inherited oaths. As the moon nears its thirteenth turn—the moment the entity becomes permanent—Astrid and Sef gather allies among smugglers, exiled priests, and one reluctant princess. In the end, Astrid must choose between destroying their own gift (the price of unbinding) or letting duty claim them both; they find a third path, transferring the binding onto the crown itself, shattering it, and choosing each other over inheritance.
about_author: Elodie Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-books before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse in the northern hills, where they keep an unreasonable number of maps.

chapters.title: Ink and Indenture
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet them copying a heretical text by candlelight, counting down their debt in ledger margins, and smuggling a letter through the Thornfell pass for extra coin. Emotional beat: weary competence masking longing for freedom.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Criers announce the gift-hunt; the abbot burns the archive and offers to sell names to save the monastery. Astrid hides one book inside their coat. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that owns them.

chapters.title: What the Mapmaker Knew
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The royal cartographer is interrogated for treason after marking anomalies on the king's seal-line. He escapes with half-burned charts pointing to Thornfell. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve.

chapters.title: Smoke Over the Pass
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Hunters arrive at the monastery; Astrid's gift flares involuntarily, lighting every candle in the scriptorium. They flee into the mountains at night. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of first escape.

chapters.title: Two Fugitives
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Astrid and Sef collide on a smuggler road, each suspecting the other of being a hunter. A grudging truce forms when his map matches her memory of the passes. Emotional beat: wary sparks of trust.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. He explains the entity wearing the king's face—it feeds on dynastic oaths and completes its binding at the thirteenth lunar turn, six weeks away. Astrid refuses to believe until she reads the burned chart. Emotional beat: dread settling into purpose.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The monastery sells her name; hunters led by Captain Veyra close in. Astrid uses smuggler knowledge to fake their deaths in a rockslide. Emotional beat: grief for the life she can never return to.

chapters.title: The Smugglers' Court
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They seek refuge with Maren Ostwick, the fence who taught Astrid the roads, now dying. Maren demands a price: carry her confession to the exiled priests of Hollowmere. Emotional beat: found family, and its cost.

chapters.title: Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The hidden priory of priests who once bound the crown. Their blind oracle confirms Astrid's gift is the old 'unbinding' kind—but warns the ritual requires a willing heir's blood. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by an impossible requirement.

chapters.title: Princess Ilseva
chapters.summary: Ilseva's POV. The king's daughter, kept drugged and docile in the palace, recognizes her father is gone. She intercepts a hunter dispatch meant for Veyra and begins her own quiet rebellion. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Veyra's Ledger
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The hunt captain discovers the crown ordered her own family's oaths harvested decades ago. She begins keeping two ledgers—one for the crown, one for the truth. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking.

chapters.title: The Salt Road Ambush
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. An ambush splits the party; Astrid's uncontrolled gift saves Sef but reveals their location to Veyra. First kiss in the aftermath, quickly regretted. Emotional beat: love as vulnerability.

chapters.title: Confession at the Shrine
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Fulfilling Maren's last request, Astrid delivers her confession—and learns Maren was her grandmother, and the debt that bound her was manufactured to hide her bloodline. Emotional beat: rage and reclamation of identity.

chapters.title: The Palace of Wax
chapters.summary: Ilseva's POV. Ilseva sneaks into the sealed throne room and finds the true king alive but hollowed, whispering her childhood name. She vows to free him. Emotional beat: filial love against horror.

chapters.title: Bargain with the Hunt
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Veyra corners the fugitives but, having read her second ledger, offers a deal: bring her proof of the entity, and she'll open the palace gates. Emotional beat: enemies becoming uneasy allies.

chapters.title: What the Gift Costs
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The oracle reveals the unbinding will consume the caster's gift forever—or their life if they hesitate. Astrid secretly prepares to pay with their life rather than lose the magic that finally makes them belong. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice born of shame.

chapters.title: Gates of Oath
chapters.summary: Ilseva's POV. Veyra opens the gates; Ilseva confronts the entity wearing her father's face and nearly kneels to it, so deep do the inherited oaths run. Sef pulls her back. Emotional beat: the seduction of duty.

chapters.title: The Throne Room
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Climax begins: Astrid reaches the hollowed king while the twelfth moon rises. The entity offers Astrid everything they've wanted—belonging, erasure of debt—if they stop. Emotional beat: temptation at its most personal.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Climax. Rather than paying with their life or gift alone, Astrid binds the entity into the crown itself using Ilseva's willing drop of blood—not as sacrifice but as choice—and Sef shatters the circlet. The king wakes. Emotional beat: triumph through refusal of false choices.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Broken Crown
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The kingdom reels; Veyra presents her second ledger to the regency council, burning the first. Ilseva refuses the throne for now, insisting on reform. Emotional beat: hard-won accountability.

chapters.title: Ledgers Closed
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid returns to Thornfell not as debtor but as founder of a new archive where gifts are taught openly. Sef asks what she'll do with her freedom. Emotional beat: peace, and the courage to want things.

chapters.title: The Road We Keep
chapters.summary: Alternating Astrid/Sef. Epilogue under a new moon: the two walk the smuggler roads together, mapping them honestly this time, delivering letters instead of secrets. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.
